summary:
# BOOK 1 of 2: The Boy Traders; Or, The Sportsman's Club Among the Boers (Harry Castlemon, Frank Nelson Series)

## Characters
- Frank Nelson: sailing-master of schooner *Stranger*; nephew of Uncle Dick; earlier commanded the whaler *Tycoon* (after Capt. Barclay deserted; was "shanghaied" earlier). Cousin of Archie Winters.
- Uncle Dick (captain of Stranger; old sailor, miner at Bendigo, meerschaum pipe).
- Archie Winters: cousin of Frank; prankster, backwoods-savvy, lasso skill, Maynard rifle, "Yankee" quips.
- Walter Gaylord: paymaster, keeps books and safe key; "Walter" rescued by Dick & Bob earlier.
- Eugene Gaylord: Walter's brother; flute player; new Henry rifle; double-barrel; bold dares.
- Featherweight (nickname), George (George Le Dell), Fred (Fred Craven), Perk (Phil Perkins), Jasper etc. = Sportsman's Club members.
- Dick Lewis: backwoods trapper, Indian yells, super-fast runner, "Human natur'!"; Bob Kelly: trapper companion.
- Mr. Baldwin: first mate; Mr. Parker: second mate; Barton: coxswain/boatswain's mate; Lucas: old boatswain's mate; Rodgers; Freas; the Doctor (negro cook); Brown (repentant sailor).
- Waters: escaped English convict, giant; struck Lucas; bribed guard; "Yankee" insults. Bob (ticket-of-leave man, with revolver); Stevens.
- Fowler: consul's clerk, "Aw!" drawl, gold eyeglass; instigator of seizure.
- Mr. Wilbur: sheep-herder, Uncle Dick's friend, station near river at Hobart Town.
- Mack (McGregor): Scotch transport-rider, driver; deserted with Walter's horse & gun.
- Mynheer Schrader: surly Boer field cornet.
- Kaffirs (4) deserted; Griquas; Zulus; chief.
- Colonel (English) sold outfit.

## Plot (in order)
1. Ch I: Captain Uncle Dick, barometer, cyclone talk; Frank explains storm. Recap: Tycoon adventures; Honolulu. Sandwich Islands 3 weeks. Hilo: surf-board dare; Archie & Eugene back down. Kilauea volcano; trappers frightened, decide to go on with Uncle Dick.
2. Ch II: Mangrove Islands; Long Tom (30-pounder) fired at natives; ship anchored; storm rises. Dick: "Human natur'!" Gale; schooner battened; cabin darkened; damage (jibboom, topmasts lost).
3. Ch III: Cyclone; Mr. Baldwin explains; Stranger dismantled; drifts toward island; Long Tom thrown overboard; shrapnel repels canoes (~300 natives). Ship of Sea Gull driven onto reef; 11 rescued.
4. Ch IV: Rescued men (escaped convicts Waters + 3 others; Waters giant). Plan: repair at Hobart Town. Frank on watch; Archie: "Van Diemen's Land" convicts.
5. Ch V: Waters swaggers, insults Mr. Parker; strikes Lucas; Dick Lewis floors Waters with handspike; master-at-arms irons him. Uncle Dick decides Japan/India dropped; plan Natal. Archie vows horse race vs Dick.
6. Ch VI: Arrival Hobart Town; Waters confirms; consul's clerk Fowler "Aw!" demands convicts; Mr. Baldwin refuses without written order. Police commissioner boat; Fowler reveals Waters' chain-gang history. Uncle Dick's bribery story (Bendigo, ounce of gold). Archie's Rocky Mountain jokes.
7. Ch VII: Mr. Wilbur's sheep station; Archie's horse race: Dick beats Eugene's horse. Melbourne trip; Archie's horse stolen by bushrangers. Fowler visits Frank in Hobart reading-room; asks about safe, paymaster Walter. Schooner returns; Frank locked in cabin; Archie is in cabin; masked convicts (Bob with revolver) seize vessel; Waters & Fowler enter.
8. Ch VIII: Frank learns plot: Fowler & Waters; convicts escaped, 3 foremast hands (Brown, Stevens, +1) joined; Sea Gull crew; Bob ticket-of-leave man. Waters orders Frank to sail to San Francisco. Frank accepts; Archie mate. Crew watch.
9. Ch IX: Fowler's plan to lure Walter down lane; Bob seizes Archie by mistake ("paymaster" in Panama hat). Archie kept prisoner. Frank tricks steamer (Yankee trick): tarpaulin, sail past at night. Archie handcuffs Waters while asleep (with Bob's tools/revolvers). Archie hid revolvers.
10. Ch X: Archie & Frank recapture schooner: Bob, Fowler, Waters ironed; Brown & crew turn; British steamer (Lt. gray-headed, Mr. Kendall midshipman) boards; Frank refuses turn over; flag dispute.
11. Ch XI: Kendall vs Archie over flag; steamer leaves; tug with Club arrives (Uncle Dick, Wilbur). Three foremast hands discharged at Hobart Town. Schooner sails to Natal.
12. Ch XII: Grahamstown; English colonel's outfit (oxen, wagon, horses, guns); McGregor "Mack" hired; lottery: Frank draws horse #3 (vicious) & heavy rifle; Archie gets thoroughbred & silver rifle. Kaffirs hired.
13. Ch XIII: Boer farm, Mynheer Schrader refuses trade; Frank repairs Griqua gun; Mack warns of lion veldt; Eugene dares.
14. Ch XIV: Eugene, Archie, Fred night in shooting-pit at fountain; "lions" fired upon; actually wild dogs (Ch XV revealed).
15. Ch XV: Archie's horse wanders into thorn bush; Mack suspicious; Kaffirs plan desertion; Mack appears to steal Walter's horse & Uncle Dick's double-barrel.
16. Ch XVI: Kaffirs & Mack deserted; Zulus demand gun; Dick Lewis's war-dance yells scare off Zulus ("medicine man").
17. Ch XVII: Zulu attack in dry stream ravine; Archie's horse killed; Frank saves Archie; spear hits Frank's haversack. Griquas return; trade; homeward; Stranger returns to Bellville; Gaylord; Conclusion: Frank lawyer; Archie civil engineer; Chase & Wilson orange plantation; Fred revenue lieutenant; Jasper Babcock cotton factor; George Le Dell Memphis; Perk steamers; Walter/Eugene plantation; Uncle Dick cabin.

Quoted: "Human natur'!"; "Ladrone Islands"; "Aw! ... weally"; "Trek!"; "I'm a little boy, am I?"; "I wasn't born."

# BOOK 2 of 2: The Yellow House; Master of Men (E. Phillips Oppenheim)

## Characters
- Kate Ffolliot: narrator, daughter of Horace Ffolliot; "pale-faced, black-haired chit"; secretary to Adelaide Fortress; lover of Bruce Deville.
- Horace Ffolliot: father; curate-in-charge at Northshire vicarage; alias Philip Maltabar; later Canon of Belchester/Eastminster; killed Stephen Berdenstein; dies in East End hall (Colville Hall).
- Alice Ffolliot: youngest sister; priggish, pious; "Be off, you little goose!" (Kate).
- Lady Naselton (Amy): gossip, matchmaker; godmother of Bruce; Naselton Hall; husband Sir? Fred Naselton (son, South America).
- Bruce Deville: master of Deville Court; ragged; beagles (Lawless, Marvel, Madam); "godmamma" = Lady Naselton; saved Olive in Switzerland (Baeren); engaged/fails with Olive.
- Adelaide Fortress (Marcia): Kate's mother; Socialist journalist; Yellow House; once lover of Horace; "Marcia" name; cabinet with photo.
- Stephen Berdenstein: South American; dead (murdered in plantation); enemy of Philip Maltabar; once loved Adelaide.
- Olive Berdenstein: sister; short, dark, plain, sallow, diamonds; wants Bruce; "Mr. Smith" detective.
- Mr. Charlsworth: churchwarden. Mr. Hewitt (schools). Harrison (tenant, traps). Mr. Berdenstein. Mary (maid). Morris. Bishop of Exchester.
- Colonel Dacre: meddlesome busybody (Belchester).
- Mr. Densham (Socialist candidate). Lady Applecorn.

## Plot (in order)
1. Ch I: Kate's family moves to vicarage near Deville Court; callers; Lady Naselton tells of "Yellow House" woman and Bruce. Father's faint reaction to "Bruce Deville."
2. Ch II: Kate sees Bruce & dogs in lane ("pale-faced, black-haired chit"); father faints near garden, hears voice "It was her voice."
3. Ch III: Father's sermon success; Bruce's dog Lawless with broken leg; Kate binds; "Ffolliot?" F's; father and Bruce clash; "closely associated with most unhappy chapter."
4. Ch IV: Storm at Yellow House; Adelaide's den; Bruce there; "Marcia!"; father enters, orders Kate out; "Marcia" flees.
5. Ch V: South American letter ("London about fifteenth") summons father to London; Bruce drops envelope same handwriting.
6. Ch VI: Lady Naselton's party; Mr. Berdenstein (millionaire, Rio); "Adelaide Fortress" name; Kate hears Berdenstein's secret.
7. Ch VII: Father missing; Kate goes to Yellow House; accuses Berdenstein; Adelaide says "No!"; father returns; Kate sees father's revolver.
8. Ch VIII: Sunday; father ill; Bishop coming; father meets Berdenstein on downs ("Welcome to England once more, Stephen").
9. Ch IX: Evensong sermon "wages of sin"; Berdenstein staggers in bleeding, accuses "Judas!"; dies in churchyard; verdict murder.
10. Ch X: Kate ill; Bruce sends roses; father to be canon.
11. Ch XI: Father admits meeting; "mad"; Kate promises silence; decides to leave.
12. Ch XII: Olive Berdenstein calls; seeks Philip Maltabar; father refuses to see her.
13. Ch XIII: father "Vengeance belongs to God"; Bruce walks Kate; Kate asks about dead man.
14. Ch XIV: Father bandaged wound; Kate meets Bruce at gate; Adelaide's sitting-room.
15. Ch XV: Olive shows photo in cabinet ("Philip Maltabar"); Adelaide denies.
16. Ch XVI: Kate sees photo: father as youth; Adelaide: "It was my father." (Kate realizes father = killer).
17. Ch XVII–XVIII: Bruce & Kate walk; Olive stays at Grant's farm; Kate's jealousy.
18. Ch XIX–XX: Adelaide tells story: she left father for theories; Kate is their child ("you are my child--and his!"). Olive arrives with Bruce.
19. Ch XXI: Father left for London; Kate learns Adelaide is Bruce's father's ward.
20. Ch XXII: Olive's compact: stay away from Bruce; "ten thousand pounds".
21. Ch XXIII–XXV: Kate avoids Bruce; Olive scorns Kate; Bruce proposes; Kate refuses ("I do not care for you").
22. Ch XXVI: Adelaide proposes trip to London; Bruce's "Olive" subplot.
23. Ch XXVII: East End (Commercial Road) glimpse of father; telegrams; father's letter from Ventnor denies.
24. Ch XXVIII: Father back at Eastminster; Bruce meets Kate in Eastminster; Olive's compact broken; Bruce proposes again; Kate accepts; Olive threatens.
25. Ch XXIX: Evensong; Olive recognises father; father confesses killing Stephen in self-defence (Stephen's knife); Olive leaves.
26. Ch XXX: Father's letter farewell (secret life); Kate follows; Colville Hall (East End) — father preaches farewell; Olive informs detective; "Mr. Smith"; father dies: "This is happiness."

Quoted: "wages of sin is death"; "Judas!"; "Oh, you are a swift judge!"; "You are my child--and his!"; "This is happiness."
